title: Mayer-Vietoris exact sequence in right derived evaluation
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with two opens U,V covering X, and let E_W^n be the nth right derived functor of evaluation of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] on the object W of X_et [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], for W in {X,U,V,U intersection V}. There are natural transformations delta_n : E_(U intersection V)^n → E_X^(n+1). For every coefficient sheaf F, the simultaneous restriction E_X^0(F) → E_U^0(F) × E_V^0(F) is injective. For each n the sequence E_X^n(F) → E_U^n(F) × E_V^n(F) → E_(U intersection V)^n(F) → E_X^(n+1)(F) → E_U^(n+1)(F) × E_V^(n+1)(F) is exact at the three interior positions; the second map is the difference of the restrictions. This asserts neither comparison with global sections on open schemes nor the vanishing consequence.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50 (lemma-mayer-vietoris), with Cohomology on Sites Lemma Tag 03F3 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-cohomology-of-open) for the identification $H^q_{\Et}(W,F)=H^q(W_{\Et},F|_W)$

proof.text: *The covering and its fibre products.* The open immersions $j_U:U\to X$, $j_V:V\to X$, $j_{U\cap V}:U\cap V\to X$ and the inclusions $k_U:U\cap V\to U$, $k_V:U\cap V\to V$ are etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), so $X,U,V,U\cap V$ are objects of $X_{\Et}$ and the inclusions are morphisms of $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Since $X=U\cup V$, the family $\mathcal U=\{U\to X,V\to X\}$ is jointly surjective, hence a covering of $X$ in $X_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (with $S=X$, both maps $\mathrm{id}_X$, and the opens $U,V$ resp. $U,U$, etc.), every fibre product $W_0\times_XW_1\times_X\cdots\times_XW_p$ with $W_k\in\{U,V\}$ is identified with the open subscheme $W_0\cap\cdots\cap W_p$, the projections becoming the inclusions; in particular $U\times_XU=U$, $V\times_XV=V$ (both projections the identity), $U\times_XV=V\times_XU=U\cap V$, and every product containing both $U$ and $V$ is $U\cap V$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50 (lemma-mayer-vietoris), proof: 'the covering X = U ∪ V'

proof.text: *Sections of an abelian sheaf: left exactness.* Let $\mathcal I$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ and consider $0\to\mathcal I(X)\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal I(U)\oplus\mathcal I(V)\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal I(U\cap V)$ with $a(s)=(s|_U,s|_V)$ and $b(s,t)=s|_{U\cap V}-t|_{U\cap V}$; $b\circ a=0$ since restriction is functorial. The sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] for the covering $\mathcal U$ of step 1 says $\mathcal I(X)\to\mathcal I(U)\times\mathcal I(V)\rightrightarrows\prod_{W,W'\in\{U,V\}}\mathcal I(W\times_XW')$ is an equalizer. By step 1 the two components on $U\times_XU=U$ and on $V\times_XV=V$ of the two arrows agree for every $(s,t)$ (both projections are the identity), and those on $U\times_XV$ and $V\times_XU$ both say $s|_{U\cap V}=t|_{U\cap V}$. So $a$ is injective, and $(s,t)$ with $b(s,t)=0$ is $a$ of a (unique) section: the sequence is exact at $\mathcal I(X)$ and at $\mathcal I(U)\oplus\mathcal I(V)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50, proof: 'This is true in the first and middle spots as I is a sheaf'

proof.text: *Surjectivity on the right for an injective sheaf.* Let $\mathcal I$ be an injective object of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and $\gamma\in\mathcal I(U\cap V)$. Index $\mathcal U$ by $\{U,V\}$ and use the identifications of step 1. Define $c\in\check{\mathcal C}^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=\prod_{(i,j)}\mathcal I(U_i\times_XU_j)$ [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex] by $c_{UU}=0$, $c_{VV}=0$, $c_{UV}=\gamma$, $c_{VU}=-\gamma$; i.e. $c_{ij}=(\varphi(j)-\varphi(i))\gamma$ with $\varphi(U)=0,\varphi(V)=1$, where $\gamma$ stands for its restriction to $U_i\times_XU_j$ whenever $i\neq j$. $c$ is a cocycle: $d(c)_{i_0i_1i_2}=c_{i_1i_2}-c_{i_0i_2}+c_{i_0i_1}$ restricted to $U_{i_0}\times_XU_{i_1}\times_XU_{i_2}$; if $i_0=i_1=i_2$ all three terms are $0$; otherwise the triple product is $U\cap V$, all three terms are multiples of $\gamma|_{U\cap V}=\gamma$ (restrictions along the projections being the identity of $U\cap V$ or the inclusions, by step 1), and the coefficient is $(\varphi(i_2)-\varphi(i_1))-(\varphi(i_2)-\varphi(i_0))+(\varphi(i_1)-\varphi(i_0))=0$. Since $\mathcal I$ is injective, $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sheaf-cech-acyclic], so $c=d(\sigma)$ for some $\sigma=(\sigma_U,\sigma_V)\in\check{\mathcal C}^0=\mathcal I(U)\times\mathcal I(V)$, i.e. $c_{ij}=\sigma_j|-\sigma_i|$. For $(i,j)=(U,V)$: $\gamma=\sigma_V|_{U\cap V}-\sigma_U|_{U\cap V}=b(-\sigma_U,-\sigma_V)$. Hence $b$ is surjective, and with step 2, $0\to\mathcal I(X)\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal I(U)\oplus\mathcal I(V)\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal I(U\cap V)\to0$ is exact. (This is Stacks' second argument; its first argument, Cohomology on Sites Lemma 093X, surjectivity of $\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal I(U\cap V)$ along the monomorphism $k_U$, would need a node of its own and is not used.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50, proof: 'Another way to prove it would be to show that the cokernel of the map I(U) ⊕ I(V) → I(U ∩ V) is the first Čech cohomology group of I with respect to the covering X = U ∪ V which vanishes by Lemmas 03OR (lemma-hom-injective) and 03OV (lemma-forget-injectives)'

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution F → I in nonnegative degrees. Apply the injective section sequence from the preceding two steps in each degree. Since its maps are restrictions, they commute with the differentials and produce a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes I(X) → I(U) × I(V) → I(U intersection V). Right derived evaluation is homology of each evaluated resolution, and homology of the finite product is the product of homologies.

*The long exact sequence.* By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] (in the abelian category of abelian groups) the sequence of step 4 has connecting maps $\delta^q:\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(U\cap V))\to\mathcal H^{q+1}(\mathcal I^\bullet(X))$ with $\cdots\to\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(X))\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^q(a)}\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(U))\oplus\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(V))\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^q(b)}\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(U\cap V))\xrightarrow{\delta^q}\mathcal H^{q+1}(\mathcal I^\bullet(X))\to\cdots$ exact; since all complexes vanish in negative degrees, $\mathcal H^{-1}=0$ and the sequence starts with $0\to\mathcal H^0(\mathcal I^\bullet(X))$. $\mathcal H^q(a)=(\mathcal H^q(r_U),\mathcal H^q(r_V))$ and $\mathcal H^q(b)=\mathcal H^q(r'_U)-\mathcal H^q(r'_V)$, where $r_W:\mathcal I^\bullet(X)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(W)$, $r'_W:\mathcal I^\bullet(W)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(U\cap V)$ are the restriction maps of complexes.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50, proof: 'the associated long exact cohomology sequence is the sequence of the statement'; homology.tex Lemma Tag 0117

proof.text: For a morphism F → G, lift it to a chain map between injective resolutions. Restriction commutes with that chain map, giving a morphism of the degreewise short exact sequences. Naturality of the homology connecting maps implies naturality in F. Homotopy uniqueness for the lifts also implies independence of resolutions. Thus the connecting maps are natural transformations between the displayed right derived evaluation functors.

mathlib_searches.verdict: No exact statement: the site Mayer-Vietoris theorem is for Ext-based H-prime, not right derived evaluation or its comparison with total derived global sections. Graded, Zariski and pro-etale results in the upstream source have different hypotheses and functors.

∃ δ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
        (evaluation _ _).obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (U ⊓ V).ι))).rightDerived n ⟶
      (sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
        (evaluation _ _).obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)))).rightDerived (n + 1),
      ∀ F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1},
        Function.Injective (fun x => (((Functor.whiskerLeft (sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology
            AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
          ((evaluation _ _).map (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk
            (A := Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι) (B := Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))
            U.ι (Category.comp_id U.ι)).op)).rightDerived 0).app F x,
          ((Functor.whiskerLeft (sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
          ((evaluation _ _).map
            (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (A := Scheme.Etale.mk V.ι)
              (B := Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) (V.ι) (Category.comp_id V.ι)).op)).rightDerived 0).app F
            x)) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ,
          Function.Exact (fun x => (((Functor.whiskerLeft (sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology
            AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
          ((evaluation _ _).map
            (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (A := Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι)
              (B := Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) (U.ι) (Category.comp_id U.ι)).op)).rightDerived n).app F
            x,
          ((Functor.whiskerLeft (sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
          ((evaluation _ _).map
            (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (A := Scheme.Etale.mk V.ι)
              (B := Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) (V.ι) (Category.comp_id V.ι)).op)).rightDerived n).app F
            x))
            (fun x => ((Functor.whiskerLeft (sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u +
            1})
          ((evaluation _ _).map
            (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (A := Scheme.Etale.mk (U ⊓ V).ι)
              (B := Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι) (X.homOfLE (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ≤ U)) (X.homOfLE_ι
            inf_le_left)).op)).rightDerived
            n).app F x.1 -
          ((Functor.whiskerLeft (sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
          ((evaluation _ _).map
            (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (A := Scheme.Etale.mk (U ⊓ V).ι)
              (B := Scheme.Etale.mk V.ι) (X.homOfLE (inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ≤ V)) (X.homOfLE_ι
            inf_le_right)).op)).rightDerived
            n).app F x.2) ∧
          Function.Exact (fun (x :
            ((sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
              (evaluation _ _).obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι))).rightDerived n).obj F ×
            ((sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
              (evaluation _ _).obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk V.ι))).rightDerived n).obj F) =>
            ((Functor.whiskerLeft (sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology
            AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
          ((evaluation _ _).map
            (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (A := Scheme.Etale.mk (U ⊓ V).ι)
              (B := Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι) (X.homOfLE (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ≤ U)) (X.homOfLE_ι
            inf_le_left)).op)).rightDerived
            n).app F x.1 -
          ((Functor.whiskerLeft (sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
          ((evaluation _ _).map
            (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (A := Scheme.Etale.mk (U ⊓ V).ι)
              (B := Scheme.Etale.mk V.ι) (X.homOfLE (inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ≤ V)) (X.homOfLE_ι
            inf_le_right)).op)).rightDerived
            n).app F x.2) ((δ n).app F) ∧
          Function.Exact ((δ n).app F)
            (fun x => (((Functor.whiskerLeft (sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u
            + 1})
          ((evaluation _ _).map
            (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (A := Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι)
              (B := Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) (U.ι) (Category.comp_id U.ι)).op)).rightDerived (n +
            1)).app F x,
          ((Functor.whiskerLeft (sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
          ((evaluation _ _).map
            (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (A := Scheme.Etale.mk V.ι)
              (B := Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) (V.ι) (Category.comp_id V.ι)).op)).rightDerived (n +
            1)).app F x)))
